hero.title: Gathering data, strengthening policy.
hero.lead: SurveyMETER is a survey, training, and research institute in Yogyakarta. Since 2002 we have run large-scale household surveys for government, international agencies, and universities.
hero.cap: Launch of the ILAS 2023 report at the Asia-Pacific Regional Conference on Population Ageing, with Bappenas, FEB UI, Lembaga Demografi, and ADB.

about.title: From the IFLS field team to a policy research institute
about.p1: SurveyMETER was founded to formalise the work of a research team with more than 15 years of experience collecting and analysing Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS) data. Our aim is accurate, reliable data for sustainable public policy.
tl.1: Founded as a foundation in Yogyakarta on 20 February 2002.
tl.2: Foundation re-established by a new notarial deed, registered with the Ministry of Law and Human Rights.
tl.3: Became a research institute: research, community assistance, and policy advocacy.
tl.4: Became PT SurveyMETER to widen work with government, the private sector, and international partners.
about.photo: The SurveyMETER team in front of the office, Maguwoharjo, Sleman.
vm.visionText: A knowledge institution that inspires and strengthens policy based on research data.
vm.m1: Run large-scale surveys and research objectively and with quality.
vm.m3: Take an active part in policy dialogue.
vm.m4: Provide technical assistance on using data and research results to policymakers and other knowledge institutions.
vm.v1: Scientific integrity: objective, high quality, independent
org.title: Organisation 2024-2028
org.history: Previous executive directors: Bondan S. Sikoki (2002-2012) and Dr. Ir. Ni Wayan Suriastini, M.Phil (2012-2024).
work.title: Three areas of work
work.note: The Indonesian government and international agencies have repeatedly trusted us with surveys, evaluations, and training.
area.impactText: Measuring the impact of government or international programmes, both ongoing and completed.
area.policyText: Assessing how well policies work, as a basis for improving programmes.
area.trainingText: Training interviewers, field staff, data editors, and cadres for partner surveys.
area.assistText: A social laboratory in assisted areas to test empowerment tools and support data-based local policy.
area.scienceText: Longitudinal household surveys with Indonesian and international researchers, some with public data.
area.reviewText: Independent studies, policy briefs, and popular writing from research results.
